To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
CD57+ T lymphocytes show a high susceptibility to apoptosis mediated by the CD3 complex and the expression of the CD57 molecule may play an important role in this susceptibility.
the CD3‐mediatied apoptosis of CD57 + T cells is associated with the increased production of active‐caspase‐3 and the expression of Fas and FasL.
the susceptibility of CD3‐mediation apoptosis of CD57 ^{+} T cells was associated with the increased expression of Fas and FasL, and the decreased expression of survivin.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the susceptibility of CD3‐indicated apoptosis of CD57 + T cells and provides new insights into the mechanism of the expansion of CD57+ memory T cells in the human immune system.
the mechanisms of CD3‐mediation apoptosis in CD57+ and regular αβ T cell subsets.
the mechanisms underlying the susceptibility of CD3‐mediatied apoptosis of CD57‐expressing T cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CD57+ T cell is more susceptible to apoptosis than the regular T cell, and this may contribute to its accumulation with age.
the CD57+ T cell subset is more susceptible to CD3/CD3ɛ‐mediated apoptosis than regular T cells.

the susceptibility of CD3‐mediation apoptosis of CD57 T cell is due to a combination of several factors including a biased TCR repertoire, low TCR expression level, and imbalance in the expression of the CD38 and CD3ζ molecules.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CD57+ T cell apoptosis may occur through a Fas‐mediated pathway, and that the expression of the CD57 molecule may not be directly related to apoptosis.

CD57+ T cell apoptosis is induced through a CD3‐mediation mechanism, and this mechanism involves the activation of the Fas/FasL pathway and suppression of anti‐apoptosis factors, which may be due to the imbalance in the expression of CD3ɛ/ζ chains.
CD57+ T cell apoptosis may contribute to the development of the CD57+ T lymphopenia observed in patients with chronic hepatitis C.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the expression of CD3ζ in CD57+ αβ T cells is much higher than that in regular αβ T cell.
the expression of CD57 on αβ T cells is not a stable phenotype, but is rather a marker of a subset that is undergoing apoptosis.

CD3+CD57+ T cells are susceptible to undergo CD3‐mediat ed apoptosis, and that this susceptibility may be due to the imbalance of CD3ɛ/CD3ζ expression, which is a characteristic feature of these cells.
